skill.name: pymc-bayesian-modeling
skill.description: Build, diagnose, validate, and compare Bayesian models with PyMC, including hierarchical models, MCMC, variational inference, and predictive checks.
skill.summary: Practical PyMC guidance for Bayesian model design, inference, diagnostics, prediction, and comparison.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 110 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, dictionary keys, or Bayesian terminology. No command execution or reconnaissance behavior was found, but the documented pickle.load example creates a medium-risk unsafe deserialization concern.

remediation.suggestion: Use a safer persistence format when possible, or require trusted files and warn that pickle.load can execute arbitrary Python code.

content.user_title: Build Reliable Bayesian Models with PyMC
content.value_statement: Bayesian analysis requires careful priors, diagnostics, and model validation. This skill guides PyMC model construction, inference, predictive checks, and comparison.
actual_capabilities: Builds linear, logistic, Poisson, time-series, and hierarchical PyMC model structures with suitable likelihoods and priors.
Provides reusable linear regression and non-centered hierarchical templates covering preparation, fitting, validation, and prediction.
Explains NUTS, Metropolis, sequential Monte Carlo, and variational inference, including when each approach fits.
Checks R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, and tree depth through included diagnostic utilities.
Compares fitted models with LOO or WAIC, evaluates Pareto-k reliability, and supports weighted prediction averaging.
Guides prior predictive checks, posterior predictive checks, uncertainty summaries, and out-of-sample predictions.
limitations: Requires a working Python environment with PyMC, ArviZ, NumPy, pandas, and plotting dependencies.
Cannot determine scientifically valid priors without domain knowledge and context from the user.
Does not guarantee convergence; complex models can require substantial computation and iterative reparameterization.
Documented pickle loading must never be used with untrusted or externally supplied files.

use_cases.title: Develop a Bayesian regression
use_cases.description: Create a complete PyMC regression workflow with informed priors, MCMC sampling, predictive checks, and uncertainty summaries.

use_cases.title: Analyze grouped experimental data
use_cases.description: Design a non-centered hierarchical model that estimates group effects through partial pooling and checks convergence.

use_cases.title: Audit production model quality
use_cases.description: Diagnose fitted models, compare alternatives with LOO or WAIC, and assess whether averaged predictions are justified.

prompt_templates.title: Build a first PyMC regression
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a PyMC linear regression for [outcome] using [predictors]. Explain prior choices, standardize inputs, and include prior and posterior predictive checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design a hierarchical model
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a non-centered hierarchical PyMC model for [outcome] grouped by [group]. Use named dimensions and explain partial pooling and hyperpriors.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose MCMC sampling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these ArviZ diagnostics: [summary]. Identify divergences, R-hat, ESS, and tree-depth problems. Recommend prioritized changes and explain each recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Compare and average models
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [model list] using LOO and WAIC. Assess Pareto-k reliability, explain uncertainty in rankings, and propose model averaging when differences are small.

output_examples.input: A beginner needs a Bayesian regression for house prices with three standardized predictors.
output_examples.output: The response defines informed priors, a Gaussian likelihood, four-chain NUTS sampling, convergence checks, and prior and posterior predictive validation.

output_examples.input: A fitted hierarchical model has divergences, low effective sample size, and an R-hat above 1.01.
output: The diagnosis identifies unreliable sampling and advises against interpreting the posterior.
It prioritizes non-centered parameterization, stronger priors, higher target acceptance, and longer chains.

output_examples.input: Two fitted models have similar LOO scores, but one has several high Pareto-k values.
output_examples.output: The comparison treats the ranking as uncertain, flags unreliable LOO estimates, and recommends validation or cautious model averaging.

best_practices: Standardize continuous predictors and document all transformations before defining priors.
Run prior predictive checks before fitting, then inspect R-hat, ESS, and divergences before interpreting results.
Use posterior predictive checks and reliable LOO or WAIC diagnostics before selecting or averaging models.
anti_patterns: Do not use flat priors automatically or choose distributions without considering the data-generating process.
Do not trust posterior summaries when chains diverge, R-hat is high, or effective sample size is low.
Do not load pickle artifacts from untrusted sources; deserialization can execute arbitrary Python code.

faq.question: Which software does this skill support?
faq.answer: It targets PyMC 5.x and ArviZ workflows. Required Python packages must be installed separately.

faq.question: Can it choose priors for my model?
faq.answer: It suggests appropriate prior families, but final choices require domain knowledge, measurement scales, and prior predictive validation.

faq.question: Does it run models automatically?
faq.answer: It provides guidance, templates, and utilities. Execution depends on the agent environment, installed packages, data, and available compute.

faq.question: How does it diagnose sampling problems?
faq.answer: It evaluates R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, tree depth, trace plots, rank plots, energy, and autocorrelation.

faq.question: Does it support hierarchical models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes non-centered multilevel templates, group-level analysis, partial pooling guidance, and diagnostics.

faq.question: Can I load saved pickle models safely?
faq.answer: Only load pickle files you created and protected. Untrusted pickle data can execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization.
